UChicago bachelor's applicant fits graduate degree pathway; minimum undergraduate GPA3.0. International
applicants accepted. Final degree/individual readiness must be reviewed. [s1] [s2]

pages;2027 capacity unconfirmed. [s1] [s7]

under Fee Waiver Weeks FAQ. [s3] [s6]

Math deadline explicitly 2027; central fee waiver page 2027 but department waiver text still 2026. [s1] [s6]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Tuition plus monthly stipend for 9-month academic year and3-month summer; numeric 2027 amount not
established. Summer-school teaching may add support. [s4]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Normally five years with satisfactory progress; previous training may shorten to four or less. Sixth year
requires request by end fall of fifth year and is not guaranteed; no support beyond sixth. [s5]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
No nationality restriction stated for ordinary Math support; international applicant aid eligibility should be
confirmed in offer. [s4]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Academic/teaching/exam/research progress required. About eight duty hours weekly during academic year.
Unsatisfactory progress can end support. [s4] [s5]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Department nominates exceptional candidates for Rice fellowships/research assistantships; no independent
incoming form identified. [s4]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Rice fellowships/RA; external awards encouraged. The department's generic NSF suggestion does not establish
this F-1 applicant's eligibility. [s4]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD85 nonrefundable, online credit card/electronic check. [s1]
Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
Current central 2027 worldwide doctoral waiver request window Oct 14-Nov 1 (already closed as of Nov 5).
Approved applicants submit by Nov 27,10:59p.m. CST; GPA3.0; letters/tests may follow by program deadline.
Match request/application email; no refunds. Math discretionary need waiver: mathgradchair@rice.edu;
qualifying named-program routes also listed. [s1] [s6]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Anthony Várilly-Alvarado
Arithmetic of K3/del Pezzo surfaces, Brauer groups, rationality. [s7] [s8]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: current preprint, year not shown · Geometric realizations of Brauer classes on K3 surfaces from
hyperkaehler contractions
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
Sarah Frei
Hyperkähler varieties, derived categories, K3/cubic-fourfold arithmetic. [s7] [s9]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2026 · A framework for Tate modules of abelian varieties under isogeny
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
David Urbanik
Algebraic and arithmetic geometry; families of varieties, Hodge theory, periods, special moduli and unlikely
intersections. [s7] [qbr3_q4] [qbr3_q5] [qbr3_q6] [qbr3_q7]
Assistant Professor, Rice Mathematics; new 2026-27 faculty.
Research evidence: 2026 · Arithmetic deformation of line bundles
With Ziquan Yang; published 7 February 2026, Mathematische Annalen 394, article 8. Mixed-characteristic deformation and
characteristic-zero lifts of line bundles.
Research evidence: 2025 · Geometric G-functions and atypicality
Duke Math. J. 174(12), 2425-2512; published 1 September 2025. Period G-functions, Galois-orbit bounds, special moduli and
Zilber-Pink.
Evidence history and corrections (earlier statements may be superseded)
 Earlier interests: Hodge theory, periods, special moduli and arithmetic geometry; recent paper metadata not yet verified.
Earlier appointment: Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Number theory
Brandon Levin
p-adic Hodge theory, Galois deformations, local models and Langlands. [s7] [s10]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2024 · Irregular loci in the Emerton-Gee stack for GL_2
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
Representation theory
Chelsea Walton
Noncommutative and quantum algebra; quantum symmetries, Hopf algebras, braided module and monoidal
categories, representation theory. [s7] [s11] [qbr2_q1] [qbr2_q2] [qbr2_q3]

Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2026 · Morita invariants of quasitriangular coideal subalgebras
With Monique Müller. Preprint 2025; revised 8 February 2026; Rice author page gives J. Pure Appl. Algebra 230 no. 3, 108210
(2026). Uses braid-group representations to study braided module categories.
Research evidence: 2025 · Division algebras in monoidal categories
With Jacob Kesten; revised 17 November 2025; author page says to appear J. Algebra and Its Applications.
Evidence history and corrections (earlier statements may be superseded)
 Earlier interests: Noncommutative/quantum algebra, categorical algebraic structures; current publication-list audit
pending.
